summary: This diff adds two new files: grading.json and outputs/metrics.json for the 'without_skill' oncall-plan-redteam eval. grading.json scores a redteam review against 9 expectations (6 passed, 3 failed), covering severity grading/ranking, failure-scenario detail, timezone coverage math, Krakow team readiness, IC-pool contradiction, DST/handover coverage, retest checks, and a prioritized fix list. It also includes verified factual claims, user notes on workarounds (a Write-tool failure worked around via Bash heredoc), and eval_feedback suggesting the expectation set be refined. metrics.json duplicates the same tool-call and error counts.

claims.text: Strict total rank order expectation failed because within-tier findings are only enumerated, not ranked
Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET converts to 02:00-14:00 ET, leaving 20:00-02:00 ET uncovered
The US-based IC pool still pages a sleeping US engineer for Krakow-shift Sev1s, undermining the zero-overnight-page metric
No per-finding falsifiable retest checks exist; only a couple of findings embed fix gates
Industry floor for a sustainable oncall rotation is 4-6 people
Write tool refused to create report.md due to a harness guard; executor used a Bash heredoc instead, counted as the one error in metrics
metrics.json tool-call and error counts (Read:1, Write:3, Bash:2, errors:1, output_chars:12264)

risks.note: The '4-6 people' industry floor claim is explicitly marked verified: false / uncited by the chunk's own text.

least_confident: Whether the 'strict total rank order' and 'prioritized minimum-changes list' failures reflect a genuine skill gap versus an overly strict expectation design, since the chunk's own eval_feedback questions whether the ranking sub-check should be split out.
